column1: # claim-ledger.tsv — one row per durable claim: id <TAB> command <TAB> expect <TAB> exit <TAB> timeout <TAB> note
# `expect` is an ERE matched against the LAST non-empty line of the command's
# combined stdout+stderr; the exit code must equal the fifth column. Both must
# hold. Rows are reviewed, committed, and refused (POLICY, exit 2) if they are
# not a single simple command (allowlisted first token, no metacharacters, no
# denied verb) — see corpus/claim-ledger.sh header §Command safety.
# R11-06 carries exit 1 on purpose: the recorded baseline of the transcript
# gate IS a firing gate (2 `xai-` prose-collision HITs, credential tripwires
# empty). A change in that line is a host-state event to re-baseline, not a
# gate defect.
# Count rows (R11-10/11, and the `(N cases)` expectations) exist because three
# committed docs carried stale numbers for these same quantities (README said
# 20 state-shape rows and a 14-case census selftest; PROVINCE said 21 rows) —
# a number a doc cites is a claim, so it belongs here.
